references.text: The book of Leviticus gives detailed laws that sacrificial animals must be without defect, including a prohibition against offering blind, lame, or injured animals to the Lord.
It forbids offering an ox or sheep with a defect to the Lord, as it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
The prophet Malachi rebukes the people for bringing blind, lame, and sick animals as sacrifices, asking whether this is acceptable to God.
Malachi condemns those who promise to give a good animal but instead offer a defective one to the Lord.
Parallel rules apply to priests with physical defects who could not approach the altar, underscoring the requirement of perfection in worship.
The Passover lamb was to be without defect, a principle that applies to all sacrificial animals offered to the Lord.
